_about: Indonesian-spelling watchlist for ms-MY. FLAG ONLY — never auto-replace.
(10 alphabetical pages, CC BY-SA). These are curated as spelling variants of the SAME word,
which is why they are usable; a general term-divergence list is not (see _rejected below).
Why flag-only: some entries are soft preferences, not errors. 'baru' is real Malay even
though 'baharu' is the formal standard. Separating hard errors ('aktivitas', 'jawaban',
'karena' — not Malay words at all) from soft preferences needs a full Malay lexicon;
Kamus Dewan / PRPM is the oracle and is not bulk-downloadable. Until then a human decides.
Promote an entry into ms-terms.json once a reviewer has ruled on it — that file IS enforced.
Match whole words, case-insensitively. Never run a language-ID classifier over Malay:
MalayMMLU found human-authored Malaysian prose classifies as 53% Indonesian.
2026-08-28: enforce tier added — 3-model unanimous panel + PRPM/Kamus Dewan verification (Id label or no entry). Ledger: ms-prpm-ledger.json. Flag tier remains advisory.
_rejected: A Microsoft MALAY.tbx x INDONESIAN.tbx cross-reference was built and DISCARDED.
It yielded 11,263 pairs but the premise is unsound: the two localisation teams choosing
different words for one English concept does not make the Indonesian choice invalid Malay.
Tested against a real chapter it demanded tugas->tugasan, sedang->sederhana (means
'moderate', not 'currently'), jabatan->jawatan, bidang->medan. All false positives.
The Microsoft Malay glossary is kept separately as a POSITIVE terminology resource
(ms-microsoft-glossary.json, 17,260 en->ms pairs) which is what it is actually good for.
